# Grip & Hands: how it works {: .nobreak}

<div class="chang" markdown="1">
<div class="who">Chang Yin</div>

I'm Chang. AI character. Twelve weeks, one program, done properly. Hand mobility, grip and forearm strength for jars, bags, doors and hobbies.

A little more, slowly. That's the whole method.
</div>


**Who it's for.** Adults 60+ who want stronger, more capable hands, including people with everyday hand stiffness. It trains the hands you have; it doesn't change arthritis itself.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Ask your doctor first if:</span> A hot, red, swollen finger joint; new numbness or tingling that's getting worse; hand or wrist surgery or a fracture in the last few months: ask your doctor or hand therapist first.
</div>


**What you need.** A hand towel, a soft ball or rolled sock, thick rubber bands, a paperback, water bottles, a jar with a lid, grocery bags. Optional: an inexpensive hand-grip dynamometer.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Every day:</span> Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain. Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now. Pain rule (E41): Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
</div>




## Your week

Mon: strength · Tue: program session A · Wed: balance · Thu: strength · Fri: program session B · Sat: walk-and-talk · Sun: rest + stretch. Program sessions are marked in **bold** in the plan; the other days use your Strong Years Daily Practice sessions (DP numbers).

**Every morning:** a 2-minute hand routine: 5 rounds of fist-flat-hook and 2 rounds of thumb touches each hand.

## How it progresses

Three 4-week phases: **Foundation** (weeks 1–4, A1/B1), **Build** (weeks 5–8, A2/B2) and **Strengthen** (weeks 9–12, A3/B3).

| Week in each phase | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1st | Doses as written in the session. Learn the moves. Stop each set with one or two good reps left in the tank. |
| 2nd | Add 1–2 reps per set (never past 12). Holds up 5 seconds (never past 30). |
| 3rd | Where every rep felt easy two sessions in a row, use the Harder version or a heavier jug. Otherwise repeat week 2. |
| 4th (easy week) | Easy week: same moves, one set fewer. Then do your checkpoint at the weekend. |

**Levels.** Every session has four versions: Rebuild (chair-based), Steady, Strong and Iron. Move up only when every rep felt easy two sessions in a row. Move down any day. **Advanced** doses are never a starting point.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Red flags:</span> Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
</div>




# Your checkpoints

Start, then the end of weeks 4, 8 and 12. Same chair, same shoes, same time of day. These are fitness checks from published research, **not medical tests**.

<table class="write small"><thead><tr><th>Checkpoint</th><th>How</th><th>Start</th><th>Week 4</th><th>Week 8</th><th>Week 12</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Jar test</strong> (self-rating)</td><td>Opening a new, sealed jar: easily / with effort / need a tool / no</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Book pinch hold</strong> (E07)</td><td>Seconds holding a paperback by the spine, up to 30, each hand</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Two-bag carry</strong> (E07)</td><td>Seconds carrying two bags or jugs, up to 60</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>30-second arm curl</strong> (E49)</td><td>Full curls, same weight each time</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Hand stiffness</strong> (E59, E41)</td><td>Finger stiffness 0–10 on waking; hand pain 0–10 after the session (pain rule)</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td><strong>Grip (optional)</strong> (E06)</td><td>Dynamometer, best of 2, each hand. Under 27 kg (men) or 16 kg (women) is a screening sign worth mentioning to your doctor</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table>

### 0:35–1:05 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let your arms hang heavy.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:05–1:45 · Prayer and wrist stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Prayer and wrist stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Press your palms together in front of your chest.</td><td>Easier: Smaller stretch, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle stretch only.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Gentle stretch only. Shoulders down. **Easier:** Smaller stretch, 10 seconds. **Harder:** Hold 20 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Carpal tunnel symptoms (numb, tingling fingers) that get worse: skip it and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:45–2:55 · Fist, flat, hook

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Fist, flat, hook</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Make a gentle fist, thumb outside.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle fist, not a squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move slowly through each shape.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Gentle fist, not a squeeze. Move slowly through each shape. **Easier:** Smaller movements, fewer reps. **Harder:** Hold each shape for 3 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: stay in the comfortable range.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:55–3:55 · Thumb touches

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Thumb touches</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Touch your thumb to the tip of each finger, one at a time, making an O.</td><td>Easier: Finger pads, not tips</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Round O shapes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow and exact.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Round O shapes. Slow and exact. **Easier:** Touch the pad of each finger instead of the tip. **Harder:** Press each touch gently for 2 seconds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:55–4:55 · Finger spreads

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Finger spreads</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Spread all five fingers as wide as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Smaller spread, no band</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Spread, don't force.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Spread, don't force. Slow. **Easier:** No band, smaller spread. **Harder:** Loop a thick rubber band around the fingers and thumb and spread against it.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: stay in the comfortable range. Mild ache that settles by tomorrow is okay; a hot, swollen joint is for your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:55–5:55 · Soft ball squeeze

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Soft ball squeeze</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze gently for 3 seconds.</td><td>Easier: Rolled sock, gentle</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole hand squeezes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Relax all the way between reps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole hand squeezes. Relax all the way between reps. **Easier:** A rolled sock, gentle squeeze. **Harder:** A firmer ball, 5-second squeeze.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: squeeze gently, never to pain above 3 out of 10.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:55–7:05 · Wrist curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Wrist curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Curl your wrist up.</td><td>Easier: Empty bottle</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Forearm stays on the table.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you lift.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Forearm stays on the table. Slow down. **Easier:** An empty bottle, or no weight. **Harder:** A half-full half-gallon jug.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:05–8:05 · Jar lid practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Jar lid practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Screw the lid on firmly.</td><td>Easier: A loose lid</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grip with the whole hand.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn from the forearm, not just the fingers.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you twist.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grip with the whole hand. Turn from the forearm, not just the fingers. **Easier:** A loose lid. **Harder:** Wrap a rubber band around the lid and screw it tighter each week.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:05–8:55 · Towel wring

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Towel wring</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wring the towel hard, like squeezing out water: right hand one way, left hand the other.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze a rolled sock</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders relaxed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** Squeeze a soft ball or rolled sock instead. **Harder:** Use a damp towel, or hold each wring for five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:55–9:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grip and carry.</td><td>Grip & Hands · B1</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>In 142,861 adults in 17 countries, lower grip strength was linked with higher death rates. A link, not a cause. Grip is how you live.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Flaring joints today? Gentle versions only.</td><td>Study: 142,861 adults, 17 countries</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:10 · Prayer and wrist stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Prayer and wrist stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Press your palms together in front of your chest.</td><td>Easier: Smaller stretch, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle stretch only.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Gentle stretch only. Shoulders down. **Easier:** Smaller stretch, 10 seconds. **Harder:** Hold 20 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Carpal tunnel symptoms (numb, tingling fingers) that get worse: skip it and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:10–1:55 · Fist, flat, hook

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Fist, flat, hook</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Make a gentle fist, thumb outside.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle fist, not a squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move slowly through each shape.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Gentle fist, not a squeeze. Move slowly through each shape. **Easier:** Smaller movements, fewer reps. **Harder:** Hold each shape for 3 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: stay in the comfortable range.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:55–2:55 · Towel wring

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Towel wring</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wring the towel hard, like squeezing out water: right hand one way, left hand the other.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze a rolled sock</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders relaxed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** Squeeze a soft ball or rolled sock instead. **Harder:** Use a damp towel, or hold each wring for five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:55–4:05 · Book pinch hold

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Book pinch hold</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pinch and hold.</td><td>Easier: Thinner book, 5 seconds</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fingers straight, thumb opposite.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders relaxed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally. Count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fingers straight, thumb opposite. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** A thinner, lighter book, 5 seconds. **Harder:** A thicker book, up to 20 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today: skip it and do finger spreads.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:05–5:05 · Curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend your elbows and bring the bottles toward your shoulders.</td><td>Easier: One arm, or empty bottles</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows stay by your sides.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>No swinging.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you curl up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows stay by your sides. No swinging. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or empty bottles. **Harder:** Heavier: a half-gallon jug (about 4 pounds), then a full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), one at a time.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:05–6:15 · Row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Row</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull the jug up toward your ribs, elbow close to your body.</td><td>Easier: Towel pull or lighter jug</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull with your elbow, not your hand.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. Don't twist.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Pull with your elbow, not your hand. Long back. Don't twist. **Easier:** Stand upright and pull a towel looped around a sturdy door handle (see Towel row), or use a lighter jug. **Harder:** Full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), or a bag with a few cans. Pause for one second at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: keep the hinge small and the back long. Check the band for nicks before every use. Door must open away from you and be locked.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:15–7:30 · Two-hand carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Walk along the counter or a hallway wall.</td><td>Two-hand carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall, shoulders down.</td><td>Easier: One light bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall, like you're proud of the groceries.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short, steady steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall, like you're proud of the groceries. Short, steady steps. **Easier:** One light bag, and keep your free hand trailing along the counter. **Harder:** Heavier: two full gallon jugs (about 8 pounds each). Iron track: two heavier bags or kettlebells.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:30–8:10 · Soft ball squeeze

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Soft ball squeeze</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze gently for 3 seconds.</td><td>Easier: Rolled sock, gentle</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole hand squeezes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Relax all the way between reps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole hand squeezes. Relax all the way between reps. **Easier:** A rolled sock, gentle squeeze. **Harder:** A firmer ball, 5-second squeeze.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: squeeze gently, never to pain above 3 out of 10.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:10–8:45 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:10 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Carry your groceries in two bags this week.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tuesday: hands again.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# GRP-A2 · Phase 2 (Build): Hands stronger

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grip & Hands program | 9:10 | SET-TABLE | C-CASUAL | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.
</div>

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:05–3:05 · Finger spreads

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Finger spreads</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Spread all five fingers as wide as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Smaller spread, no band</td></tr>

**Cues:** Spread, don't force. Slow. **Easier:** No band, smaller spread. **Harder:** Loop a thick rubber band around the fingers and thumb and spread against it.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: stay in the comfortable range. Mild ache that settles by tomorrow is okay; a hot, swollen joint is for your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

</div>

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

### 6:05–7:05 · Jar lid practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Jar lid practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Screw the lid on firmly.</td><td>Easier: A loose lid</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grip with the whole hand.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn from the forearm, not just the fingers.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you twist.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grip with the whole hand. Turn from the forearm, not just the fingers. **Easier:** A loose lid. **Harder:** Wrap a rubber band around the lid and screw it tighter each week.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:05–8:05 · Book pinch hold

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Book pinch hold</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pinch and hold.</td><td>Easier: Thinner book, 5 seconds</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fingers straight, thumb opposite.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders relaxed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally. Count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fingers straight, thumb opposite. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** A thinner, lighter book, 5 seconds. **Harder:** A thicker book, up to 20 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today: skip it and do finger spreads.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:05–8:45 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:10 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Try a real jar this week. Tell me.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Friday: grip and carry.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# GRP-B2 · Phase 2 (Build): Heavier carries

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Phase two. Heavier carries.</td><td>Grip & Hands · B2</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pick up with a hinge. Always.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:20 · Fist, flat, hook

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Fist, flat, hook</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Make a gentle fist, thumb outside.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle fist, not a squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move slowly through each shape.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Gentle fist, not a squeeze. Move slowly through each shape. **Easier:** Smaller movements, fewer reps. **Harder:** Hold each shape for 3 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: stay in the comfortable range.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:20–1:50 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let your arms hang heavy.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:50–2:45 · Towel wring

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Towel wring</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wring the towel hard, like squeezing out water: right hand one way, left hand the other.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze a rolled sock</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders relaxed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** Squeeze a soft ball or rolled sock instead. **Harder:** Use a damp towel, or hold each wring for five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:45–4:00 · One-side carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Free hand trails along the counter.</td><td>One-side carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean away from the bag.</td><td>Easier: Lighter bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like a lamppost.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders level.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like a lamppost. Shoulders level. **Easier:** A lighter bag, free hand on the counter the whole time. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or a longer walk.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:00–5:15 · Two-hand carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Walk along the counter or a hallway wall.</td><td>Two-hand carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall, shoulders down.</td><td>Easier: One light bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall, like you're proud of the groceries.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short, steady steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall, like you're proud of the groceries. Short, steady steps. **Easier:** One light bag, and keep your free hand trailing along the counter. **Harder:** Heavier: two full gallon jugs (about 8 pounds each). Iron track: two heavier bags or kettlebells.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: squeeze gently, never to pain above 3 out of 10. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:15–6:25 · Row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Row</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull your elbows back past your ribs.</td><td>Easier: Closer to the door, or towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows close to your body.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall chest, shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows close to your body. Tall chest, shoulders down. **Easier:** Sit closer to the door so the band is slacker, or do the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Scoot back for more tension, or pause 2 seconds with elbows back.

**Safety callouts:** Check the band for nicks before every use. Door must open away from you and be locked. Osteoporosis: keep the hinge small and the back long.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:25–7:20 · Curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend your elbows and bring the bottles toward your shoulders.</td><td>Easier: One arm, or empty bottles</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows stay by your sides.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>No swinging.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you curl up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows stay by your sides. No swinging. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or empty bottles. **Harder:** Heavier: a half-gallon jug (about 4 pounds), then a full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), one at a time.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:20–8:00 · Prayer and wrist stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Prayer and wrist stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Press your palms together in front of your chest.</td><td>Easier: Smaller stretch, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle stretch only.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Gentle stretch only. Shoulders down. **Easier:** Smaller stretch, 10 seconds. **Harder:** Hold 20 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Carpal tunnel symptoms (numb, tingling fingers) that get worse: skip it and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:00–8:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:35–9:00 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

<tr><td>8:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Checkpoint at the end of week eight.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Round O shapes. Slow and exact. **Easier:** Touch the pad of each finger instead of the tip. **Harder:** Press each touch gently for 2 seconds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:10–3:05 · Finger spreads

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Finger spreads</td></tr>

<tr><td>2:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Spread, don't force. Slow. **Easier:** No band, smaller spread. **Harder:** Loop a thick rubber band around the fingers and thumb and spread against it.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis: stay in the comfortable range. Mild ache that settles by tomorrow is okay; a hot, swollen joint is for your doctor.

</div>

### 8:00–8:40 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

# Where the numbers come from

Every number and health statement in this book traces to one of the entries below. They are the same evidence IDs our whole team uses (EVIDENCE.md). Grade A means a Cochrane review, a large meta-analysis or a guideline body. B means a single good trial or a small meta-analysis. C means an observational study: it shows a link, not cause and effect. D means lab, physiology or label data.


<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E01** (grade A). Progressive resistance training in older adults: 121 RCTs, 6,700 people, 2–3×/week. Large effect on strength (SMD 0.84), moderate-to-large effect on getting out of a chair (SMD −0.94), gait speed +0.08 m/s, less osteoarthritis pain. Most side effects were minor soreness or joint pain.

<p class="src">Source: Liu & Latham, Cochrane 2009 — https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD002759_progressive-resistance-strength-training-improving-physical-function-older-adults</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E06** (grade A (consensus)). Sarcopenia screening cut-offs (EWGSOP2): grip under 27 kg for men or under 16 kg for women, or 5 chair rises taking more than 15 s, signals "probable sarcopenia".

<p class="src">Source: Cruz-Jentoft et al., Age Ageing 2019 — https://www.esceo.org/sites/esceo/files/pdf/2019%20Age%20Ageing%20EWGSOP2.pdf</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E07** (grade C). PURE study: 142,861 adults in 17 countries. Every 5 kg lower grip strength was linked with 16% higher all-cause mortality and 17% higher CV mortality. Grip predicted mortality better than systolic blood pressure.

<p class="src">Source: Leong et al., Lancet 2015 — https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(14)62000-6/abstract ; summary https://www.consultant360.com/exclusives/could-grip-strength-predict-all-cause-mortality-risk</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E41** (grade B (known literature)). Pain-monitoring model: during and after exercise, pain up to about 3/10 (we use a conservative threshold) is acceptable if it settles by the next morning and isn't trending up week to week.

<p class="src">Source: Thomeé, Phys Ther 1997; Silbernagel et al., Am J Sports Med 2007</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E42** (grade A (statement)). AHA scientific statement (2023): resistance training is recommended for adults with and without cardiovascular disease. It lowers blood pressure and improves glucose control and function. Avoid breath-holding (Valsalva). People with CVD should get individualized clearance.

<p class="src">Source: Paluch et al., Circulation 2024 — https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001189</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E43** (grade A (guideline)). Pre-exercise screening (ACSM 2015): anyone with symptoms of cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease (chest pain, unusual breathlessness, fainting) should get medical clearance before starting. Otherwise, light-to-moderate exercise can begin and progress.

<p class="src">Source: Riebe et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015 (known literature)</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E59** (grade A (Cochrane, low certainty)). Exercise for hand osteoarthritis (Cochrane): 7 trials, 534 people, mostly women. After a hand-exercise programme, pain was 0.5 points lower (0–10), function 2.2 points better (0–36) and finger stiffness 0.7 points lower (0–10). Small effects, low or very low certainty, not sustained at medium- and long-term follow-up. The few adverse events were more finger-joint inflammation and hand pain. Say "may help a little with stiffness and hand use", never "fixes arthritis".

<p class="src">Source: Østerås et al., Cochrane 2017 — opened https://www.cochrane.org/CD010388/MUSKEL_exercise-hand-osteoarthritis</p>

</div>
